subject: OrbisAI hyperscaler bench: follow-up and concrete next-tests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@orbisai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-30T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: OrbisAI hyperscaler bench: follow-up and concrete next-tests

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can prioritize work on both sides: 

1) What we covered (recap)
- OrbisAI goals: reduce hallucination for clinical content and match current latency targets for the user-facing workflow (95th pct < 300ms).
- You asked for a head-to-head against the hyperscalers you mentioned: Vertex/Vertex Inference, Bedrock (selected foundation models), and one open-model baseline you already run in-house.
- We shared an initial pass of prompt seeds and a lightweight synthetic test harness. I attached the seed prompts (orbis_seed_prompts_v1.csv) and a short PDF with our initial aggregate deltas (hyperscaler_prelim_summary.pdf).

2) Proposed evaluation scope (concrete, minimal first run)
- Metric set: exact-match for structured outputs where applicable, hallucination rate (free-text hallucination classification using your rubric), and a small regression set for factuality (50 high-priority clinical Qs).
- Context window: test at 1k and 4k windows to match your product flows.
- Throughput/latency: single-request p95 on standard instance types you run.
- Cost proxy: token cost + instance/minute estimate (for internal benchmarking only).

3) Asks from Orbis (what we need back)
- A brief prioritized list of the top 50 clinical prompts you care about (we included seeds; if you can reorder/annotate, we’ll use that).
- Any existing hallucination labeling rubric or sample annotations.
- A preferred test window for re-run (we can schedule a compute slot next Tue/Wed).

4) Our immediate next actions (what we’ll do)
- Run the minimal head-to-head (1k + 4k) across the three vendor variants and our optimized open baseline.
- Produce per-prompt deltas with a simple hallucination flag and a short executive summary for your team.
- Schedule a 30-minute results readout the week after the run.

If that plan looks good, I’ll reserve a 6-hour compute window next Tue (4/2) and kick off the baseline runs. If you prefer Wed (4/3) we can do that as well.

Thanks again — timing / any missing context?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0174
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OrbisAI hyperscaler bench: follow-up and concrete next-tests

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications before you run: 

- Hallucination definition: we mark a response as hallucinated if it contains assertions that contradict the (gold) clinical note or adds unsupported novel facts. We have ~120 labeled examples; I can share 30 now (sensitive redactions applied).
- Priority prompts: I’ve annotated the attached CSV in Drive with asterisks; top 20 are the immediate priority.
- Latency baseline: our current 95th pct target is 300ms in prod, but for the bench we care about relative deltas at p95.

We are fine with the Tue 4/2 slot — please go ahead and schedule. Procurement looped in for any contractual/commercial follow-up after we see the results.

Samantha Price
Head of Product, OrbisAI
Samantha.price@orbisai.com

Folks — forwarding Orbis thread. Key asks they confirmed: use their 20 top prompts (we have seed CSV), run at 1k/4k windows, return p95 deltas + hallucination flags. They’ll share 30 labeled examples we can use as a small validator.

Questions for next steps:
- Can data science quickly build a lightweight hallucination classifier using their 30 labeled samples as a checkpoint? It doesn't need to be perfect — just consistent across all variants for the bench.
- Ops: I plan to reserve a 6-hour slot Tue 4/2 (we said Tue). What priority instance types should we test for meaningful vendor comparison (e.g., A100 for open baseline, vendor-provided optimized instances for hyperscalers)?

Also attaching a short note about scope in the Drive (link above). Planning to produce an exec one-pager for Samantha within 48 hours of run completion.

—Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OrbisAI hyperscaler bench: follow-up and concrete next-tests

Thanks Ben — quick plan from my side:

1) Hallucination classifier (short-lived)
- Prod ML will spin up a lightweight binary classifier trained on the 30 labeled examples from Orbis + 70 synthetic negatives (we'll seed via template perturbations). Expected turnaround: 36 hours. Output: per-response flag + confidence score.

2) Instances & run shape
- Test set:
  - Vendor A (Hyperscaler-1): managed model variant on their provisioned instance (we'll use the config they recommended in call).
  - Vendor B (Hyperscaler-2): standard Bedrock-like endpoint (we'll map to the closest throughput spec).
  - Open baseline: our optimized quantized run on A100 (8x batch/continuous KV).
- For cost proxy we’ll capture instance-minutes + token counts.

3) Deliverables + timing
- Tue 4/2: run window (Ben to reserve).
- Wed 4/3: initial per-prompt CSV with hallucination flag + latency p95 deltas.
- Thu 4/4: 15-min dry readout with Orbis followed by formal 30-min readout Fri 4/5 for execs.

4) Risks & mitigations
- Small labeled set for hallucination classification — we’ll treat the classifier as advisory only and include manual spot checks for top-5 prompts.
- Vendor config mismatches — ops to document exact instance configs and request provider-confirmed settings.

I’ll book the readout slots once Ben confirms the run window. Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
